name: Do outdoor living projects need drainage under pavers or slabs?

mainEntity.name: Should drainage be built into a patio or hardscape installation?
mainEntity.text: Should drainage be built into a patio or hardscape installation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Drainage should be part of the outdoor living plan from the beginning. Even a beautiful patio can fail if water has nowhere to go, especially near the house or under a covered area. Proper slope, drainage channels, and runoff management help protect the slab, pavers, and adjacent foundations. On smaller Los Angeles lots, where backyards are often tight and hard surfaces are extensive, drainage problems can show up quickly after the first heavy rain. A good builder will think about where water moves before setting finish elevations. That can prevent pooling, soil erosion, and long-term maintenance issues.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes. Proper drainage under pavers, slabs, and patio covers helps prevent pooling, soil movement, staining, and damage to adjacent structures. Drainage is especially important on sloped or compact lots.
